newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks to see more gains, profit-taking likely.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks to see more gains, profit-taking likely.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks enter the final week of colonial rule in record territory and could push higher on Monday as handover euphoria takes hold, although some investors may be tempted to take profits, brokers said.
China's move to tighten its grip on red chips could dampen sentiment but brokers said the measures had been discounted and may affect only smaller, less well-connected China-backed firms.
"People are just buying on handover frenzy. They think China will make the market go higher to show bullish sentiment to the world," said Dharmala Securities technical analyst Alex Wong.
"I think we will see more upside."
The Hang Seng Index staged its biggest point rally ever on Friday, rising 647.87 points to an all-time high of 15,154.36.

"There will be some short-term profit-taking but it will not go down too much," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities. He said the market should be well-supported by a liquidity flow into the market from mainland investors.

"I think there will be some short-term worries about red chips but I don't expect the selling pressure to last long," So added. "Some of the measures had been expected by the market and not all of the red chips will be affected by the measures."
